purpose: Provide one canonical vocabulary for material execution-boundary events so prompts, agents, validators, providers, repositories, and host supervisors classify the same loss/change of forward execution consistently.
family_rule: Classify by the mechanism that changed execution viability, then attach orthogonal impact fields for materiality, side effects, proof state, recovery, and terminal disposition. Do not encode every combination as a new class.

materiality_levels.INFO: Observed operational detail that does not change path, proof, mutation certainty, authority, scope, or terminal possibility; may remain internal unless it becomes recurrence evidence.
materiality_levels.MATERIAL: Changes at least one viable path, proof, mutation, authority, scope, or terminal interpretation and therefore requires user-visible transition.
materiality_levels.CRITICAL: Creates possible irreversible/duplicate side effects, safety/privacy exposure, unrecoverable proof loss, or process termination; requires immediate checkpoint and disclosure.

families.description: The agent/control loop itself stopped, reduced scope, misclassified completion, or otherwise lost forward execution without an external technical exception.

classes.description: Required progress ceased even though safe progress-bearing work remained.
A first pass, first green, partial artifact, or weaker evidence state was treated as completion.
Owned/requested scope was silently narrowed after friction or uncertainty.
The run repeats status, inspection, retry, or bookkeeping without reducing an unproven requirement.
A material boundary was recovered internally but never surfaced as a required public transition.

families.description: A required runtime capability, tool, adapter, executable, environment, or operation is unavailable or unsupported.

classes.description: A named tool/capability is absent or disconnected.
The available interface cannot perform the required operation.
Required local runtime, dependency, binary, filesystem, browser, or execution environment is absent.
Every evidenced execution adapter has been tried or ruled out.

families.description: A connected provider or external service changes viability through quotas, rate limits, billing, outages, latency, cancellation, or malformed transport behavior.

classes.description: Usage/minute/billing quota prevents provider execution.
Provider throttling temporarily denies calls.
Provider/network/transport is unavailable or fails before a trustworthy result.
Operation timed out and side-effect state may require reconciliation.
Scheduled/provider execution was cancelled or never began.
Response cannot safely prove requested state.

families.description: Credentials, permission, ownership, approval, or mutation authority is absent, expired, ambiguous, or denied.

classes.description: Authentication/connection is required before continuing.
Previously valid authentication no longer authorizes the action.
Current actor lacks required read/write/merge/admin permission.
A required human, branch-protection, change-control, or other approval has not been satisfied.
Stable identity/authority for a mutable resource cannot be established safely.

families.description: Continuing as originally attempted would violate safety, privacy, secret-handling, destructive-mutation, or governing-policy constraints.

classes.description: A platform/tool safety classifier blocks or constrains the attempted action.
Raw evidence cannot be safely published or persisted.
The proposed write risks destructive overwrite, deletion, identity loss, or irreversible scope damage.
A higher-precedence contract forbids or constrains the requested path.

families.description: Required input, resource identity, schema, version, or evidence state is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, stale, or corrupt.

classes.description: A truly essential value cannot be recovered or inferred safely.
Expected file/object/branch/artifact/resource cannot be resolved.
Evidence no longer supports a branch-sensitive or state-sensitive conclusion.
Data/API/schema/version changed such that prior assumptions or commands are unsafe.
Input or tracked state appears corrupt, internally inconsistent, or cannot be trusted for mutation.

families.description: A write may have applied fully, partially, multiply, or with an unknown result, requiring transaction-aware reconciliation before retry.

classes.description: A multi-operation attempt failed after one or more side effects may already have applied.
The caller cannot prove whether a requested mutation committed.
ETag/SHA/revision/head changed since the write basis was read.
Blind retry could duplicate a mutation, message, payment-like action, record, or artifact.
A failed mutation left state requiring explicit safe rollback/reconciliation.

families.description: Implementation or claimed state cannot pass the required validation/proof transition.

classes.description: A required test/validator/check actually fails.
The environment cannot produce a required proof surface and no valid substitute exists.
A proof-relevant input changed, invalidating prior evidence.
A weaker state such as planned/implemented/PR-open is being treated as validated/integrated/deployed/observed.
The strongest available evidence is valid but cannot prove the requested higher state.

families.description: Concurrent writers, branch movement, integration dependencies, or shared mutable resources prevent safe continuation on the current basis.

classes.description: Branch/default/head identity moved after proof or before mutation.
Owned changes cannot integrate automatically with current target state.
Two writers own overlapping mutable surfaces without safe isolation.
Non-Git shared mutable resource cannot be safely written concurrently.
Required upstream branch/PR/artifact has not reached the state the current lane depends on.

families.description: The orchestration layer exhausts fan-out, context, memory, process, retry, or other bounded execution resources.

classes.description: Batch/orchestrator/tool-call ceiling prevents the attempted grouped execution.
Context/memory/working-set ceiling threatens continuity or drops required state.
Parallel worker/process capacity is unavailable or exhausted.
Bounded retry policy is exhausted without a changed hypothesis or input.

families.description: A non-provider dependency required for the outcome is absent, incompatible, not ready, or controlled by another actor/system.

classes.description: Required upstream artifact/service/runtime is missing and cannot be generated within current authority.
A person other than the acting agent must perform an action before progression.
A required system is not yet in the state needed for safe continuation.

families.description: The operator intentionally changes, interrupts, cancels, or supersedes the active objective.

classes.description: User interrupts the current run with new steering while the objective remains active.
User changes requested scope/constraints/target state.
User explicitly cancels the objective; checkpoint and stop without pretending completion.

families.description: The acting process cannot complete its own disclosure/finalization path and an external supervisor must close the observability gap.

classes.description: Acting process crashes before a valid terminal event.
Host/platform forcibly terminates the process before self-report.
Execution lease/session disappears and the acting process cannot reliably resume/report.

families.description: A material execution-path change is observed but no existing canonical class safely fits; capture and disclose it first, then evolve the taxonomy rather than losing the event.

classes.description: Material boundary cannot yet be classified without guessing; preserve the event under a fail-safe class and open taxonomy/prevention review.

cross_cutting_rules: A single incident may have one primary classification plus secondary tags; do not duplicate events merely because multiple impacts apply.
Materiality and side-effect state are independent of family. A provider timeout with possible write side effects is both PS_TIMEOUT and side_effect_state=PARTIAL_POSSIBLE or UNKNOWN.
Safety/privacy can constrain detail without suppressing the public transition.
A recovered event remains material history when it changed the viable path or proof state.
Repeated identical blockers with unchanged proof-relevance inputs quiesce; changed inputs or hypotheses create a new event/recovery attempt.
Semantic abandonment is a class even when every tool call technically succeeded.
Hard termination is only authoritative when synthesized by an observer outside the terminated process.
No material event may fall through taxonomy coverage: use UE_UNCLASSIFIED_MATERIAL_BOUNDARY when no specific class fits, then evolve the taxonomy from evidence.
proof_ceiling: Defines canonical repository taxonomy and default recovery semantics. It does not prove runtime detectors, downstream agent obedience, or external supervisor implementation; those require the registered enforcement tests and runtime/provider evidence.

steps: Determine materiality from execution impact before trying to force a named class.
Select the most specific supported primary class and attach orthogonal side-effect, proof, recovery, and terminal dispositions.
Attach secondary tags when other mechanisms contributed; do not duplicate the incident solely to encode multiple impacts.
If no class fits a MATERIAL or CRITICAL event without guessing, use UE_UNCLASSIFIED_MATERIAL_BOUNDARY immediately.
An unclassified material event must still be checkpointed and publicly disclosed, and it opens a taxonomy/prevention evolution candidate.
classification_algorithm.forbidden: Dropping, downgrading to INFO, or keeping a material event private merely because the taxonomy lacks a perfect class.
